text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

---There is internal crisis in Denmark's opposition Conservative Party after revelations at the weekend that the new leader Per Stig Moeller lied to journalists about a 30-year-old drunken-driving offence. Moeller, a former environmental minister and writer of literary and philosophical works, was appointed Conservative leader last week to replace Hans Engell, who resigned after being found by police with a blood-alcohol level well over legal limits after a minor car accident.

---Saturday opening for banks in Denmark will soon be a reality as pay negotiations between the employers and staff in the financial sector near a successful conclusion, with agreement close on time-off in lieu arrangements.

--- The Social Democrat mayor of Copenhagen suburb Brondby denies any involvement in 115 fans of the local Brondby football club's move to join the party en masse with the aim of exerting pressure on local politicians to fund a modernisation of the club grounds. A mysterious, unknown sponsor paid the block party subscription for the fans - Brondby is a leading Danish soccer club and current champions in the local super league.
--- Denmark's second biggest bank Unidanmark has built up up a war chest of some three billion crowns for possible future takeovers of smaller local banks.

--- Leading Danish combine harvester manufacturer Dronningborg Industries is to move production of electrical wiring for its agricultural machinery to Italy to cut costs and improve competitiveness. It is also considering moving other activities abroad.
